title: Metric Curation and Backfill Playbook
author: Nora Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook defines Redwood's standard process for curating new metrics, enforcing cardinality and cost controls, and performing safe historical backfills. It centralizes decisions about metric naming, metadata, ownership, retention, and automated backfill tooling so dashboards and alerting remain reliable and cost-predictable.

Scope:
- Application and inference service metrics (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, StatsD exports)
- Derived metrics stored in time-series DB (TSDB) and aggregated counters in analytic store
- Dashboard and alert backfills for retrospective incident analysis

Goals:
1) Prevent high-cardinality churn that causes cost spikes.
2) Ensure every metric has a single responsible owner and lifecycle.
3) Provide a repeatable, auditable backfill process with safety checks.
4) Maintain dashboard integrity and historical comparability when schemas change.

Key definitions:
- Metric manifest: YAML document describing metric identity, owners, retention, and backfill policy.
- Curated metric: metric approved for long-term retention and dashboards.
- Ephemeral metric: short-lived diagnostic metrics (TTL 7 days) used for debugging.

Required metadata for every new metric (metric manifest fields):
- name (canonical): string, kebab-case, prefix by service (e.g., inference.request.latency_ms)
- description: human-readable purpose and measurement semantics
- unit: ms | count | bytes | ratio | bool
- owner: oncall alias or team (team-slug)
- cardinality_class: low | medium | high (see cardinality guidance)
- retention_days: integer
- curated: yes | no
- backfill_policy: none | partial | full (see backfill matrix)

Example metric manifest (YAML):
---
name: inference.request.kv_cache_hit_rate
description: Fraction of requests that used a cached KV prefix
unit: ratio
owner: eng-serving-runtime
cardinality_class: low
retention_days: 365
curated: yes
backfill_policy: partial
---

Cardinality guidance and limits:
- Low: <= 50 unique tag combinations per minute. Allowed for curated metrics.
- Medium: 51-1,000 combinations per minute. Require explicit justification and quota.
- High: >1,000 combinations per minute. Disallowed for curated metrics; allowed as ephemeral only with TTL 7 days and a scheduled deletion job.

Enforcement rules (engineered):
1) New metric manifests must be checked by CI linter (see metric-lint job).
2) TSDB ingestion path rejects curated metrics without an approved manifest.
3) Automatic alerts created when a metric’s cardinality grows 50% week-over-week.
4) High-cardinality tags (user_id, session_id, prompt_hash) are forbidden on curated metrics. Use hashed-binned versions only.

Metric curation workflow (steps):
1) Developer creates metric instrumented in code and adds metric manifest in the same PR.
2) PR triggers metric-lint: validates naming, required fields, and cardinality_class.
3) Observability owner reviews and assigns curated|ephemeral status.
4) If curated: add to curated-metrics registry (single source of truth) and schedule long-term ingestion.
5) If ephemeral: set TTL=7 days and annotate in manifest for automatic deletion.

Prometheus / OTel example instrumentation:
- Prometheus client (Go):
  CounterVec{name: "inference_requests_total", labels: []string{"model", "route"}}
- OTel metrics exporter: attach resource attributes: service.name, service.instance, deployment_env

Backfill policy and decision matrix:
- none: never backfill (common for ephemeral or cheap synthetic metrics).
- partial: backfill key aggregates (daily or hourly) for up to N days based on storage and CPU budget.
- full: run full historical reconstruction (only for high-value SLO metrics).

Backfill decision table (example):
| Metric Type | Curated? | Backfill allowed | Max days | Approval needed | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| SLO latency p95 | yes | full | 365 | VP Eng or SRE | High priority for incident analysis |
| Ingest-rate per model | yes | partial | 90 | Observability team | Aggregate-only backfill recommended |
| Debug histogram unique prompts | no | none | 0 | N/A | Do not backfill ephemeral metrics |

Backfill runbook (safe procedure):
1) Create or update metric manifest with backfill_policy and owner.
2) Open a backfill run request in the telemetry pipeline (Backfill Service). Include rationale, time range, and estimated cost.
3) Observability approves and assigns a run owner.
4) Dry-run: run backfill against a sample week in a staging TSDB namespace and validate checksum parity for aggregates.
5) If dry-run passes, schedule backfill in a maintenance window (prefer low-traffic hours).
6) Monitor ingestion throughput, storage growth, and alert if estimated cost > budget.
7) On completion, update dashboards and CI checks to reference the curated metric.
8) Close the change and record the run in the backfill audit log.

CLI examples (Backfill Service):
# submit a dry-run for two weeks
redwood-telemetry backfill submit --metric inference.request.latency_ms --start 2024-11-01 --end 2024-11-15 --dry-run

# run full approved backfill
redwood-telemetry backfill run --id bf-2025-004 --priority low

Safety checks and automated guards:
- Dry-run mandatory for full backfills.
- Circuit breaker: abort if ingestion rate exceeds 120% of expected or if disk growth exceeds 20% above projection in first 2 hours.
- Cost cap: enforce daily cost budget per backfill request; auto-terminate when budget is exhausted.
- Rollback: backfill writes to a namespaced partition that can be dropped if anomalies are detected.

Monitoring and observability for backfills:
- Dashboard: Backfill Manager (Grafana) showing active jobs, ETA, bytes written, and cost-to-date.
- SLI: Backfill success rate >= 99% for dry-run and >= 95% for production runs.
- Alerting: PagerDuty to telemetry-oncall on job failures, cost overruns, or checksum mismatches.

Retention and legal considerations:
- Default retention for curated metrics: 365 days.
- Sensitive tags: any metric containing PII-like identifiers must be rejected and routed to Security for redaction.
- For restricted customers, apply tenant-level retention override via manifest field retention_override: {days: N, reason: text}.

Ownership and lifecycle operations:
- Owners must respond to metric review requests within 5 business days.
- Owners should run a quarterly audit to identify unused metrics (zero or near-zero ingestion for 90+ days).
- Decommissioning steps: remove instrumentation, mark manifest curated:no, and schedule a deletion job.

Automation checklist (CI / infra integrations):
- metric-lint: validates manifests on PRs (enforced).
- curated-metrics registry: single JSON index automatically consumed by ingestion pipelines.
- backfill-service: authenticated API with RBAC mapped to oncall/team roles.
- cost-estimator: included in backfill requests to provide projected GB and $ cost.

FAQ (short):
Q: Can I add model_id as a tag on a curated metric?
A: Not without going through cardinality review. Prefer model_family or model_bucket tags.

Q: Who approves full backfills?
A: Observability + SRE lead or VP Eng for high-cost/long-range runs.

Appendix: Example linter error and resolution
- Error: "Label 'user_id' disallowed for curated metrics"
  Fix: Replace with 'user_bucket' generated at app-level (e.g., user_bucket = hash(user_id) % 100) and update manifest cardinality_class to medium with justification.

summary: Playbook for metric lifecycle: manifest requirements, cardinality limits, curation workflow, safe backfill runbook, enforcement, and ownership.
